producerAndConsumer.fact: The concrete Templates.Tests assembly embeds template-baselines.json, compiles the Shared helpers, imports PrepareForTest.targets, and references the MCP, Web.Client.ItemTemplates, Web.ItemTemplates, and Web.ProjectTemplates producer projects.

The area README documents four template packages in the configuration's NonShipping directory. The captured web producer explicitly declares PackageId Microsoft.DotNet.Web.ProjectTemplates, IsShippingPackage=false, and generated project content, including the Blazor server/client project outputs. This is a declared producer graph, not observed package output.

The build target produces the ArtifactsNonShippingPackagesDir, TestTemplateCreationFolder, and CustomTemplateHivePath assembly metadata. Installer discovery reads that NonShipping directory locally, or '.' when the installer's helix environment flag is set. The actual Helix payload composition was not inspected.

Both CreateProject overloads await EnsureTemplatingEngineInitializedAsync. Shared assembly attributes install an assembly fixture and disable test parallelization. The static success flag bypasses subsequent installation after a successful initialization in that loaded test assembly. It is not a per-generated-file or per-request lookup.

The real baseline theory reaches CreateProject before template generation. Initializer discovery snapshots matching packages before asserting their count and running its verification/install commands.

normalSourceScaleAndFrequency.frequency: One installation/discovery on the normal successful serialized initialization path per loaded test assembly. The flag is assigned only after installation succeeds; failures leave it false. No actual retries, repeated suite runs, cross-assembly multiplier, or caller concurrency were observed or invented.
normalSourceScaleAndFrequency.successfulControlFlow: Four cannot-find verification calls, four package-install calls when the existing count assertion passes, then three can-find verification calls: eleven source-level RunDotNetNew calls. These are not observed process launches or elapsed-time evidence.
normalSourceScaleAndFrequency.algorithmicBoundary: For D wildcard-enumerated files, the predicate can inspect up to 21 ordered prefixes per file and short-circuits on a match. D is not established by the four-result assertion. No measured comparison count, allocation count, or timing is claimed.

contracts.equalityVersusPrefix: The inner operation is Any with StartsWith(..., StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase), not equality-based Contains. Full package filenames have version/extension suffixes. An equality HashSet of the retained prefixes would not implement this predicate. No invented package filename is needed for that semantic distinction.
contracts.overlap: The actual retained array includes the unversioned Microsoft.DotNet.Web.ProjectTemplates prefix as well as thirteen more-specific historical Web.ProjectTemplates prefixes. A file matching multiple prefixes still appears once per outer enumeration entry because Any returns one Boolean. See prefix-contract-017.json for the exact ordered values and coverage pairs.
contracts.order: Any evaluates prefixes in array order. The outer enumeration's matching order is materialized by ToArray and later drives sequential logged installations. No ordering guarantee is inferred for Directory.EnumerateFiles itself. Reordering or deduplicating the package-result collection is not justified by this finding.
contracts.duplicatesAndMutation: The retained prefix literals are distinct and private. The readonly field does not itself make array elements immutable, but the complete captured owner contains no element mutation or exposure. Overlapping prefixes are not duplicate outer results. No result deduplication is present.
contracts.evaluation: Directory.EnumerateFiles and Where remain deferred until ToArray. Path.GetFileName(p) is evaluated inside the prefix predicate, possibly more than once for an outer file. Hoisting it is a separate possible local seam, not a validated material optimization or an equality-membership fix.
contracts.exceptionsAndSideEffects: The existing hive can be deleted before discovery. Enumeration/materialization occurs before the no-match InvalidOperationException, the four-count assertion, and any verification/install command in InstallTemplatePackages. Initialization success is recorded only after all of that completes. These ordering and failure boundaries must not be silently moved.
contracts.lifetime: The retained prefix array and success flag belong to the loaded helper's static lifetime. Each discovery creates a local result array; the source does not repeatedly rebuild a per-file set or expose a persistent mutable lookup to generated applications.

materialityDecision.positiveFinding: There is a genuine linear prefix scan nested in package-file enumeration, including repeated basename extraction in the predicate.
materialityDecision.whyNotAdvance: The card's usual equality-set substitution is semantically inapplicable. The real source bounds the retained prefix table to 21 and puts the work in successful assembly initialization rather than recurring generated-application execution. It documents/asserts four selected packages, but does not establish a large wildcard-candidate directory or repeated successful reinitialization. No material end-to-end benefit follows from these sources alone.
materialityDecision.notAColdLocationOnlyRejection: The decision uses the actual predicate, producer graph, success cache, assembly fixture/parallelization declarations, selected-count contract, and distinction between candidates and retained files, not merely the test-directory location.
notClaimed: No assertion that prefix scanning is negligible or slower/faster than an alternative.
No assertion that eleven tool invocations dominate elapsed time.
No fabricated packages, directory size, repeated initialization workload, benchmark, or measured no-gain outcome.
No duplicate-by-card, duplicate-by-snapshot, or alias disposition.
